title: "First Steps"

## Helloworld example

The following pattern is used in `main.c`:

```c
if ( strncmp( configuration.command, "helloworld", 10 ) == 0 ) {
	/* helloworld() function is defined in feature.h and implemented in feature.c */
	helloWorld();
}
```

Command-line example:

```bash
./freud.exe --debug -f images/input/image.jpeg -c helloworld
```

## Configuration structure

The command-line parser stores values in a `Config` structure:

```c
#define MAX_FILE_COUNT 10
#define MAX_LENGTH_COMMAND 25
#define MAX_ARGUMENT_COUNT 5

typedef struct _config {
	int debug_mode;
	char command[MAX_LENGTH_COMMAND];
	char* filenames[MAX_FILE_COUNT];
	char* arguments[MAX_ARGUMENT_COUNT];
} Config;
```

Important fields in `main.c`:

- `configuration.command`
- `configuration.filenames`

## Where to code

- Declare feature prototypes in `src/features.h`.
- Implement features in `src/features.c`.
- Add implemented feature names in `freud.manifest`.

Example:

```text
helloworld
dimension
```

## Recommended issue order

1. Tutorial
2. Statistics
3. Colors

See [Milestones and Issues](../Features/Features.qmd) for local specs.

## Test your feature

Before running commands, build and install the project:

```bash
cmake -B build
cmake --build build
cmake --install build
```

Then test with:

```bash
./freud.exe --debug -f <input file> -c <command>
```

## VS Code run configuration

You can also update `.vscode/settings.json` `cmake.debugConfig.args` values to test another input file and command from the VS Code Run action.
